overall_summary: Core relationship and self-respect content (like unpinning chats or deleting memories) perform moderately, but family-focused and universal emotional life lessons (Maa, Papa, calling loved ones) have significantly outperformed romantic heartache in views and engagement, signaling a massive pivot opportunity toward broader emotional storytelling.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos about parents, siblings, and calling loved ones (e.g., 'आज किसी अपने को Call कर लेना' with 286 views, and 'माँ जब पूछती है' with 216 views) heavily outperformed niche romantic heartache shorts.
winning_patterns.action: Incorporate broader emotional relationship dynamics and family bonds alongside core romantic self-respect themes.

winning_patterns.evidence: Early self-respect posts focused on specific digital actions like archive folders (23 views) and keyboards (20 views) drove steady baseline traffic.
winning_patterns.action: Maintain high-specificity micro-actions when returning to digital breakup/self-respect themes.

weak_patterns.pattern: Generic Romantic Sadness without Actionable Hooks
weak_patterns.evidence: Abstract late-night or one-sided love concepts like 'रात के ख्याल और अधूरा इंतजार' dropped to single-digit views (6 views).
weak_patterns.action: Avoid vague, abstract heartbreak tropes; ground every emotional concept in a concrete, relatable daily object or interaction.

weak_patterns.evidence: Recent repetitive daily iterations of removing profile tags and status list checks (e.g., 0-4 views) suffered from diminishing returns.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid repeating identical digital boundary-setting tropes back-to-back.
